newsitem.title: USA: Most US stock index futures end up, cash-led rally.
newsitem.headline: Most US stock index futures end up, cash-led rally.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures closed mostly higher after a cash-led rally pushed most contracts to fresh session highs in the latter half of pit trade, traders and floor analysts said.
"There is just a lot of cash being put to work," one Standard & Poor's 500 futures trader said.
"It was our late balloon move -- very light offers and spotty buying from commission houses," another trader said.
One floor trader speculated that most funds would not outperform the S&P cash index in January, and were now scrambling to mark up portfolios before the end of the month.

March S&Ps extended gains by five points in the last hour and a half of pit trade. Most traders said March's spike to the daily high of 788.25 -- through key resistance at 784.60 -- should have been generated more activity.
"A lot of technicians had to cover short positions, because we really breezed through some key areas, but volume was pretty light," one floor trader said.
Futures volume was estimated at 84,000 contracts.
"It's disappointing volume, but these are leveraged instruments and when they rally so much in such a short time that just scares people," another futures source said.
Traders did not cite arbitrage buy or sell programs for the market's sharp move.
Fair value for March S&Ps was at 3.35 points to cash, with arbitrage buy programs at a premium of 5.00 points and arbitrage sell programs 1.70 over.
Most traders are looking for buying in the cash markets to continue on Friday, and said March S&Ps could possibly test the all-time high of 799.70 before the week was over.
The rally in S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures did not spill into the Nikkei pit where March Nikkeis remained sharply lower. The contract closed down 400.0 at 17,950.0.

At the end of pit trade, March S&Ps were up 9.65 points at 787.95, KCBT Value Lines were up 4.10 at 707.55, NYSE Composites were 4.30 higher at 413.40, Midcap 400s were up 2.00 at 265.70 and Nasdaq 100s were 18.25 points higher at 919.25.
